items.text: We switched our onboarding checklist to a shared doc last quarter and it made a huge difference. New hires get a day-one email with the link, and the doc walks them through accounts, equipment and who to ask about what. Our office manager says she used an AI assistant to draft the welcome blurb, which saved a bit of time but still needed a human pass. Honestly the biggest win was just having one place everyone could see. I'd recommend it to any small team. If you want the template, it's on our intranet under People Ops.

items.text:
I've been on the fence about upgrading my phone for months, so I figured I'd write down what finally pushed me over. The battery on my old handset barely made it past lunch, and two of my most-used apps had started crashing on launch. I read a comparison roundup that an automated tool had put together, and it was actually pretty useful once I checked the prices myself. The trade-in offer through my carrier covered about a third of the new device, which felt fair. Setup was painless: contacts and photos moved over in under an hour.

The one thing I'd flag is the case situation. The new model is a slightly different size, so none of my old accessories fit, and that added maybe forty pounds I hadn't budgeted for. If you're thinking about switching, wait for a sale weekend if you can.

Overall I'm glad I did it. The camera alone was worth the upgrade, and I'm no longer hunting for a charger by mid-afternoon. If anyone's weighing the same decision, my advice is to check the trade-in value first, then decide.
